name: Green Gables Inc
old_description: Green Gables Furniture is where rugged American craftsmanship meets undeniable style. Built in the USA from real solid wood, every piece is designed to feel substantial, authentic, and impossible to ignore. From bold reclaimed barnwood to rich live-edge hardwoods and refined contemporary designs, Green Gables creates furniture with character, presence, and the kind of quality that only gets better with time.
about:
Green Gables Furniture traces its roots to Bradford, Illinois, where a family-owned operation began building furniture out of a three-car garage in the 1980s. The company remains family owned today, carrying forward the same work ethic and commitment to craftsmanship that defined its early days.

Today the company produces solid wood furniture entirely in the United States, working with reclaimed barnwood, live-edge hardwoods such as walnut, cherry, hickory, and white oak, and incorporating steel elements. Each piece is handcrafted, emphasizing natural grain, knots, saw marks, and the character of the materials. Collections range from rustic Western styles to clean contemporary designs, all built to highlight the authenticity of the wood.

Green Gables serves the residential furniture market, supplying both retail dealers and end consumers who furnish homes with its collections.

The company says its differentiation lies in blending traditional woodworking techniques with fresh design ideas, using reclaimed timbers and live edges to create furniture that gains character over time. The goal, unchanged since the garage days, is to build honest, durable pieces meant to be passed down through generations.

about:
Green Leaf Solar operates from Columbia, Missouri. The company is owned by Ryan Roe, who brings a mathematics background to system design. The founding year is not publicly disclosed.

The firm provides turnkey solar photovoltaic installations for homes and businesses. Its services include identifying all available incentives, rebates, and financing options to minimize payback periods, sometimes with zero money down. The installation team, led by chief troubleshooter Martin Podolak and solar technicians Alex and Carlos, backs each project with a 10‑ to 30‑year parts warranty, a 10‑year "Done Right" installation guarantee, and a five‑year labor warranty on part failure. Sales manager Jay Hasheider, a former utility renewable‑energy specialist with over three decades of experience, supports customer acquisition and education.

Green Leaf Solar serves residential and commercial customers in the Columbia area. Its client base includes homeowners seeking to reduce electricity bills and businesses aiming to hedge against rising energy costs. The company emphasizes a low‑risk approach, handling incentive paperwork and system design so that customers can adopt solar without upfront capital.

The company states that its differentiation lies in eliminating risk for the property owner, securing the shortest possible payback through exhaustive incentive research, and standing behind installations with long‑term warranties and a dedicated service team. Its approach is built on reliability, dependable pricing, and exceptional service, as outlined by the ownership team.

name: Green Mountain Semiconductor, Inc.
old_description: GMS specializes in Custom Analog, Digital & Mixed Signal design.
about:
Green Mountain Semiconductor, Inc. was founded in 2015 by three colleagues in Burlington, Vermont. The company began as a collaborative project among friends and evolved into a professional design organization focused on semiconductor solutions.

The firm provides custom analog, digital, and mixed-signal design services, with deep expertise in memory design including DRAM, SRAM, and emerging non-volatile memories. It offers a full flow from early technology development through test chips and test programs, specializing in compute-in-memory architectures, neuromorphic processors, and high-speed PHY interfaces such as LPDDR4/4X/5 and SPI/QPI. All design work is performed by its own employees at its Burlington office, and the team has experience in advanced nodes including 7 nm TSMC.

Green Mountain serves aerospace and defense, medical devices, and high-performance computing markets. In aerospace, it develops radiation-hardened chips that process sensor data in situ at low power. For medical devices, it creates low-power integrated circuits for patient monitoring and diagnosis, including neuromorphic edge-computing IP. The company has executed development contracts with the National Science Foundation and NASA, the latter for a family of rad-hard neuromorphic processors.

The company differentiates itself through its patented technology in commodity memory architecture, error correction, and in-memory high-parallel data processing, holding seven patents in compute-in-memory. It emphasizes a one-stop-shop approach for implementing complex algorithms into proven silicon, and maintains CMMC 2.0 certification.

about:
Gulf Side Fabricators, LLC operates from Broussard, Louisiana, on the Gulf Coast. The company was founded in October 2010 by industry veterans with over two decades of hands-on experience who were dissatisfied with prevailing quality standards.

The shop specializes in custom metal fabrication, including ASME-certified pressure vessels (U and R stamps), process piping to B31.3, and offshore/onshore piping systems. It runs a 24,000-square-foot campus that includes a dedicated carbon-steel facility and a separate exotic-alloy facility for stainless steel, super duplex, copper-nickel, and aluminum. Welding capabilities cover FCAW, GMAW, SMAW, and GTAW, supported by nesting software that the company says cuts material waste by up to 30 percent. In-house hydrostatic testing and full documentation packages are standard.

Gulf Side says it differentiates itself through a “Louisiana Pride” culture that invests in advanced technology, separate material streams to avoid cross-contamination, and a quality system built to the industry’s most demanding safety standards rather than minimum compliance.

name: H3 Plastics LLC
old_description: At H3 Plastics, we’re more than a supplier – we’re your partner. We strive to offer quality containers, real customer service, and flexibility for your needs. We make rigid packaging the easiest part of your business.
about:
H3 Plastics LLC is a family-owned rigid packaging manufacturer based in American Fork, Utah. The company launched in 2020 during the height of the COVID-19 bottle shortage, when an urgent need for packaging created a business culture centered on speed, quality, and responsive customer service. Although young, the business draws on decades of experience in manufacturing, construction, and engineering from its founders, instilling a culture of hard work, reliability, and long-term partnerships.

H3 produces both stock and custom plastic containers using Injection Stretch Blow Molding (ISBM), Reheat Blow Molding (RHB), and Injection Blow Molding processes. The facility runs modern blow molding platforms suited for small to mid-sized volume programs, working primarily with PET, HDPE, and post-consumer recycled (PCR) blends. In-house capabilities include design engineering, tooling management, finite element analysis, 3D prototyping, and integrated quality inspections covering gram weight, neck finishes, wall thickness, and leak testing. For hot-fill applications, the company offers MOQ flexibility down to 25,000 units.

The company serves health and nutrition, food and beverage, personal care, cosmetic, pet care, and household chemical markets. Customers range from medtech and specialty food brands to personal care companies, all supported by a dedicated design team and assigned representatives.

H3 differentiates itself through its family-owned values—hard work, reliability, quality control, and pride—and through certified quality systems (SQF and IMS). Sustainability is engineered into operations via lightweight designs, PCR material options, reusable packaging solutions, and energy-efficient auxiliary systems.

name: Haake Manufacturing Co
old_description: We’re not just sheet metal fabricators. We’re professional problem solvers ready to help solve your complex metal part challenges.
about:
Haake Manufacturing Co. was founded in 1948 by Fred C. Haake Sr. and his wife Elfriede in a St. Louis garage as a small tool-and-die shop. The German-trained machinist started with a single punch press and a commitment to quality that quickly earned the trust of local manufacturers. In 1963, the second generation—Fred Jr. and Lorraine Haake—relocated the operation to De Soto, Missouri, adding a company-owned trucking fleet to guarantee on-time delivery. Today, the fourth-generation family business is led by Jay Rieker and operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility in De Soto.

The company provides precision custom sheet metal fabrication entirely under one roof. Core processes include CNC laser cutting (up to 10,000 watts), CNC punching, combined punch/laser processing, CNC press brake forming with six-axis back gauges, metal stamping using AIDA cells up to 160 tons and auxiliary presses from 5 to 150 tons, robotic MIG/MAG welding of steel, stainless steel, and aluminum, and a fully automated powder coating line with six-stage wash, infrared pre-processing, and zirconium pretreatment. Secondary services such as assembly, hardware insertion, and metal finishing coordination deliver turnkey components.

Haake serves manufacturers across the United States from its central U.S. location, with a historical customer base that includes aerospace firms such as McDonnell Douglas and a broad range of Midwest industrial companies. The shop handles short-run prototypes through long-run production volumes, emphasizing just-in-time delivery programs that support inventory management and cash flow.

The company differentiates itself through integrated, in-house capabilities that eliminate supplier handoffs, a central location enabling two-day shipping to either coast, ISO 9001:2015 certification with reported defect rates of 292 PPM for fabrication and 0 PPM for powder coating, and a 99% on-time delivery record. Low operating costs powered partly by solar energy and a domestic supply chain focus further support cost competitiveness and reshoring efforts.

The company differentiates itself through its U.S.-based design and manufacturing, NIST-traceable calibration services, and the ability to deliver fully custom systems — from mechanical and electrical engineering through firmware, testing, and calibration — under one roof. Its products carry UL Listing, and the firm holds a U.S. government CAGE code (0H2P8) for federal procurement.

about:
Haven Steel Products began building its production facility in Haven, Kansas, in 1968 and started producing spring steel components the following year. The privately owned company was founded as a fabricator for the agricultural, construction, and trailer industries, and has since expanded to a second plant in McKenzie, Tennessee.

The company operates more than 200,000 square feet of production space across its two sites, offering forging on presses up to 1,000 tons, hot forming with natural gas and induction furnaces, eight quench-and-temper heat-treat lines, powder coating, a 30 kW fiber laser with bevel capability, in-house tooling, CNC machining, and a growing fleet of Kuka robots. Recent investments include two 700-ton forging presses, a 36-inch belt furnace, a Flex CNC, and a 34,000-square-foot warehouse in Kansas.

Haven Steel supplies heat-treated and tempered components to major OEMs and short-line manufacturers in agriculture (tillage parts, rotary cutter blades), construction (landscaping and mowing components), trailer (leaf springs, weight-equalizing hitch springs), railroad (wear plates), recycling (chopper knives), grounds keeping (aerator knives), playground equipment, and patio furniture.

The company emphasizes full traceability from raw steel through every process, maintains an ISO 9001:2015 quality system with ASM and FEMA membership, and holds calibration records for a minimum of three years. Its proprietary Ultra Tuf Coatings™ slurry coating is said to extend the service life of wear parts by three to five times.

about:
Heltronics Inc. was established in 2008 in Reading, Pennsylvania, situated in Berks County with convenient access to Routes 222, 422, and I-76. The company operates as a contract manufacturer specializing in electromechanical and box build assemblies.

The firm provides a full suite of assembly services, including electromechanical assembly, box builds ranging from trailer-sized units to small power supplies, cable and wire harness fabrication, control panel and cabinet assembly, rework and refurbishment, and engineering and product support. Its facility is UL certified for the U.S. and Canada and staffed with IPC‑certified personnel (standards 610/620), supporting production needs from prototype runs to high‑volume monthly orders.

Heltronics serves OEMs and EMS companies across automotive, aerospace, industrial, medical, nuclear, and power and energy sectors, as well as electromedical diagnostic and electrotherapeutic device manufacturers. Customers range from startups requiring small prototype batches to large enterprises with recurring high‑volume demand.

The company emphasizes quality and customer support, holding ISO 9001:2015 certification through Dekra and membership in the Wire Harness Manufacturing Association. Its stated philosophy is to never compromise on quality, deliver quick turnaround times, and make the customer’s production goals its own.

The company positions itself as a full-service apparel contract manufacturer capable of handling projects from sample to volume runs.

name: Hess Equipment Solutions
old_description: Hess Equipment Solutions has obtained national certification as a Women's Business Enterprise by Women’s Business
about:
Hess Equipment Solutions is based in St. Louis, Missouri. The company traces its roots to 1946 when Earl Hess began selling Berkel slicers and scales from a van. The business, originally known as Hess Meat Machines, was formally established in 1950 and expanded to a shop and warehouse on Gravois Avenue by 1961. In 2022, Rachel Herren became sole owner, and the firm earned national certification as a Women’s Business Enterprise through the Women’s Business Enterprise National Council (WBENC). It remains family‑owned and woman‑led.

Today Hess operates as a distributor and service provider for commercial kitchen and food‑processing equipment. Its product portfolio includes cooking, baking, smoking, weighing, labeling, and frozen‑dessert systems from brands such as Berkel, Southern Pride, Carpigiani, Mettler Toledo, Henny Penny, Hollymatic, Fri‑Jado, and Jaccard. The company also offers equipment repair, preventative‑maintenance plans, 24/7 emergency service, consulting, and training programs. It serves customers across Nebraska, Kansas, southern Illinois, Missouri, and Iowa.

Hess targets food‑retail, food‑service, and food‑processing operations. Its client base includes supermarket chains, butcher shops, convenience stores, restaurants, caterers, and other institutional kitchens. The firm points to long‑standing partnerships with manufacturers — such as a 40‑year run as a top‑10 Berkel distributor and a Henny Penny Service Excellence Award in 2020 — as evidence of its industry standing.

The company says its founding mission was to replace hand tools with reliable equipment, and its current differentiation rests on a combination of deep product knowledge, round‑the‑clock technical support, and a partnership model that aims to reduce downtime and improve bottom‑line results for food‑service operators.

Hi-Tek Electronics Inc. was founded in 1983 in Canton, Massachusetts.

The company distributes a wide range of electronic components, including capacitors, resistors, connectors, semiconductors, magnetics, electromechanical hardware, and thermal management products. Beyond distribution, Hi-Tek offers value-added services such as kitting (assembling bill-of-materials kits), lead forming, custom LED arrays, custom cable assembly, and dock-to-stock inventory programs. It holds authorized franchised distributor agreements with numerous discrete and passive component manufacturers.

Hi-Tek’s customers include original equipment manufacturers, cable assembly houses, and other distributors serving the consumer, commercial, military, and medical electronics markets. The company also supports applications in telecommunications, LAN infrastructure, power magnetics, and DC/DC power conversion.

Hi-Tek emphasizes design-in assistance, where its representatives work with engineers to identify alternative components that reduce production costs. The firm also conducts intensive product training workshops to educate customers on new technologies.

name: High-Purity Silicon America Corporation
old_description: In a field driven by the demand for quality - where purity is measured in "parts per trillion" - HSA has established itself as an industry leader. With a relentless pursuit of the highest level of excellence in every phase of corporate growth and development, HSA is committed to the "never-ending process" - the Continuum of Quality. We strive to understand and meet the needs of our employees, customers and neighbors. We continually look for ways to improve our processes, procedures, people, and products; because we realize that quality is a never-ending process. We strive to become the industry's preferred supplier of Polysilicon by satisfying our customer's needs for product performance, technical service and on-time delivery.
about:
High-Purity Silicon America Corporation (HSA) operates from Theodore, Alabama. The company was incorporated in 1996 as Mitsubishi Polycrystalline America Corporation, a wholly owned subsidiary of Mitsubishi Materials Corporation. It later became part of the SUMCO group of companies.

HSA manufactures polycrystalline silicon (polysilicon) in reduction furnaces. The facility also produces silicon tetrachloride and trichlorosilane as byproducts, which serve as raw materials for epitaxial semiconductors and fiber optic cables. Quality analysis includes floating zone conversion to single crystal silicon, photoluminescence detection of dopants at parts-per-trillion levels, and ICP mass spectroscopy for metallic impurities. Additional analytical capabilities cover gas chromatography, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and ICP atomic emission spectroscopy for saline product purity.

The company supplies semiconductor manufacturers and fiber optic cable producers. Its polysilicon targets the semiconductor industry, while its byproduct saline products feed epitaxial semiconductor and fiber optic cable supply chains.

HSA emphasizes a "Continuum of Quality" philosophy, describing quality as a never-ending process. It aims to become the industry's preferred polysilicon supplier by meeting customer requirements for product performance, technical service, and on-time delivery.

about:
Hino Motors Manufacturing U.S.A., Inc. is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hino Motors, Ltd. of Japan and a Toyota Group company, headquartered in Marion, Arkansas. The parent company has spent four decades as Japan's top-selling manufacturer of medium- and heavy-duty trucks, also producing buses, diesel engines, and Toyota's FJ Cruiser and Land Cruiser Prado.

In the United States, the company assembles medium-duty Hino trucks at its Mineral Wells, West Virginia plant, while its Marion, Arkansas facilities stamp and machine axles, knuckles, and suspension components for the Toyota Tacoma, Tundra, and Sequoia. A parts distribution center in Mira Loma, California supplies genuine service parts to distributors across Latin America and the Caribbean. Operations span nine locations in five states, encompassing more than 2 million square feet of manufacturing space and employing over 1,000 people. The West Virginia plant has produced over 50,000 Hino trucks and recently added a custom factory paint shop in partnership with Axalta.

The company serves the automotive and commercial-vehicle sectors, providing original-equipment components to Toyota and complete trucks under the Hino brand. Its aftermarket division supports Latin American and Caribbean distributors with service parts.

Hino emphasizes manufacturing excellence and customer-focused innovation, citing the Axalta paint partnership as raising the bar for the commercial-truck industry.

about:
Hinrichs Fine Woods originated in 1993 in Roca, Nebraska, with the goal of producing higher-quality cabinetry than competitors. The company began by building custom cabinets and furniture using solid wood, along with antique furniture restoration and repair, emphasizing wood joinery over mechanical fasteners and applying four coats of finish where others used three.

Today the shop operates from a 2,400-square-foot facility where it produces custom kitchen cabinets, bookcases, entertainment centers, bath cabinets, and other solid-wood furniture. All pieces feature inset, flush doors and drawers in traditional styles such as Mission, Shaker, and beaded face frames, with dovetailed drawers and premium hinges and guides. The restoration service refinishes antiques by hand—avoiding chemical dipping—to preserve joints and grain, then applies four coats of finish inside and out.

The company serves homeowners and collectors seeking custom cabinetry and heirloom restoration, delivering pieces built to last generations. Hinrichs Fine Woods differentiates itself by exceeding customer expectations through superior materials and craftsmanship—using wood joints instead of screws and nails, hand-stripping finishes, and applying four coats of finish inside and out.

about:
Holsen Solar was founded in 2018 in Fargo, North Dakota, by Ben Holsen, who drew on a background in entrepreneurship and technology to establish a full-service electrical contracting and solar company. The business remains headquartered in Fargo and operates as a licensed electrical and building contractor serving eastern North Dakota and western Minnesota.

The company designs, permits, installs, and warranties all projects in-house without subcontractors. Its services include rooftop, ground-mount, pole-mount, and tracking solar arrays; Level 2 EV charger installations; permanent architectural LED lighting (Gemstone residential and Haven commercial); battery backup systems using Tesla Powerwall, Franklin WH, and EG4 units; and energy management via Span smart panels and Emporia monitoring. As of the latest figures, the firm has completed over 200 projects and employs a team of 16 licensed electricians and certified installers.

Holsen Solar serves residential homeowners, farmers, small businesses, municipalities, and apartment developers across its service area. Commercial solar work is available statewide in both North Dakota and Minnesota. Recent projects include a 25 kW commercial rooftop system in Fargo, a full-roof commercial array on a metal building in Moorhead, and a complex three-story residential Gemstone lighting installation in Pelican Rapids, Minnesota.

The company emphasizes that the people who sell a system are the same people who install and service it. Its stated differentiators include holding master electrical and contractor licenses in both states, performing all work under its own permits, providing transparent pricing with detailed breakdowns, guaranteeing on-time completion, and offering a comprehensive in-house labor and materials warranty backed by manufacturer warranties. Local knowledge of utilities, cooperatives, inspectors, and weather conditions is cited as a key advantage.

old_description: We source and supply new, obsolete, and hard-to-find board-level electronic components — all independently tested at ISO/IEC 17025-accredited labs. Every order is certified, compliant, and backed by our 90-day quality guarantee.
about:
Honest Components, Inc. is based in Tampa, Florida, and operates as a woman-owned small business certified by the U.S. Small Business Administration. The company is led by President Jackie Schwab, who brings over 30 years of sales leadership in the electronic components industry. Founded on the principle that honesty and integrity create lasting partnerships, the business focuses on supplying obsolete and hard-to-find board-level electronic components to customers where reliability is essential.

The company maintains a line card of over 50,000 board-level components from manufacturers such as AMD, Intel, and Texas Instruments, covering connectors, capacitors, microcontrollers, and memory chips. Honest Components provides sourcing, procurement, and testing services, leveraging a global network of vetted suppliers. Every order undergoes third-party authentication at independent laboratories accredited to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 and AS6171, including visual inspection, X-ray imaging, decapsulation, solderability, and functional testing. The firm reports more than 200,000 authentic components supplied and over 50 combined years of industry experience among its team.

Honest Components serves aerospace, defense, medical, healthcare, and industrial sectors, supporting OEMs, contract manufacturers, and government contractors. As an ITAR-registered entity and a member of the Government-Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP), the company is authorized to manage U.S. defense-related components and actively combats counterfeit parts in the supply chain.

The company differentiates itself by bearing the cost of independent third-party testing on every order, backing shipments with a 90-day form-fit-function guarantee, and maintaining certifications including ISO 9001:2015, AS9120B, and WOSB status. Its mission centers on transparency, risk-based quality processes, and enabling customers to maintain production schedules and extend the life of legacy systems.

name: Howard Foods Inc
old_description: Our Sweet Pepper Relish is made with the plumpest, sweetest red bell peppers, while our Hot Pepper relish is made with red bell peppers and green peppers. Or try our Classic Green Tomato Piccalilli with the sweet and savory taste like your great grandmother used to make, made of green tomatoes, red peppers, onions, brown sugar, cider vinegar and a secret blend of spices.​
about:
Howard Foods Inc. operates from Danvers, Massachusetts, where its sales office has been based since 1990. The company traces its origins to the early 1890s when John F. Howard and his wife Margaret began producing relishes in the barn behind their Bradford home, drawing on recipes developed for Howard's Haverhill hotels. The business was formally incorporated after Howard sold it to Arthur D. Dickson in 1924, and a year later merged with the C.E. Chapin Company (founded 1872) to consolidate production in a Haverhill plant. Subsequent owners included ERE Industries, John Labatt Limited, and Campbell Soup Company (Canada) before the current ownership group acquired the brand in 1990.

The firm manufactures a line of shelf-stable condiments that includes Sweet Pepper Relish, Hot Pepper Relish, Green Tomato Piccalilli, Ham Glaze, and Garlic and Onion Seasoning Juices. Production follows the original late-19th-century formulations, which the company says have never been altered.

Howard Foods serves retail grocery, foodservice, and e-commerce channels primarily in the New England region.

The brand's differentiation rests on its uninterrupted recipe heritage — the 1900 Grand Prix award in Paris for purity and quality is still cited — and on a positioning that emphasizes natural ingredients, simplicity, and a "homemade" taste maintained across more than 130 years.

about:
Hunt & Noyer Furniture was founded in 2013 in the Village of Clarkston, Michigan. The company takes its name from the surnames of founder Kyle’s parents, DesNoyer and Huntoon, honoring a Midwestern family lineage of generations of hardworking craftsmen. The small business began with a commitment to tradition and the belief that quality furniture should be passed down.

The workshop designs and handcrafts a range of furniture including benches, dining tables, consoles, cabinets, seating, and upholstered pieces, with a specialty in walnut. Beyond its standard collection, the company accepts custom one‑off commissions for private homes as well as large‑scale public and corporate projects. It also partners with interior designers, offering a trade discount on current collection items. Production is described as thoughtfully designed and built for generations, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Hunt & Noyer serves residential clients, interior designers, and commercial and public‑sector customers. The company’s differentiation rests on a scientific, engineering-based approach that emphasizes problem prevention over detection. about:
Imricor Medical Systems was co-founded by Steve Wedan in 2006 and established in the Twin Cities area, with its headquarters in Burnsville, Minnesota. The company began with Wedan and three other pioneers aiming to bring interventional magnetic resonance (iMR) technology to the catheter ablation market. It is publicly traded on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX:IMR).

The company develops and manufactures MR-compatible products for interventional MR procedures, including capital equipment such as the NorthStar Mapping System and the Advantage-MR EP Recorder/Stimulator, as well as single-use devices like the Vision-MR Ablation Catheter 2.0, Vision-MR Diagnostic Catheter, and steerable sheaths. Operations are based in a Burnsville facility housing research, development, quality, and commercial teams.

Imricor serves the cardiac ablation, electrophysiology, and interventional cardiology markets, supplying hospitals and cardiac centers worldwide. Ear molding is a comfortable and straightforward process which usually takes 6 weeks.
about:
Infant Ear Molding of New Hampshire, LLC operates from Fremont, New Hampshire. The clinic was founded by Dr. Emily Hurst, who holds a Doctor of Science degree from Massachusetts College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences and has a background in pediatric plastic surgery. Recognizing that many families lacked access to noninvasive ear correction, she established the practice as the first clinic in the state dedicated solely to infant ear molding.

The company provides a noninvasive, nonmedical ear molding service that uses a malleable splint to gently reshape an infant's ear cartilage while it is still pliable, typically before the cartilage hardens around three months of age. The treatment process usually spans six weeks and is designed to correct prominent or misshapen ears without surgery or anesthesia.

The service is aimed at parents of newborns and infants with congenital auricular deformities.

Dr. Hurst's specialization in pediatric plastic surgery and the clinic's singular focus on ear molding differentiate it from general medical practices. The approach leverages a window of cartilage malleability to achieve lasting results, potentially sparing children from future psychosocial distress and surgical procedures.

Its differentiators include the only Hi‑Rel ESCC‑certified thin‑film platinum sensors, end‑to‑end development from concept to after‑sales support, and a commitment to producing varying volumes quickly.

old_description: The Dickinson Family was one of the largest producers in the area and made salt for more than 120 years. The region was the leading producer of salt in the country, with more than 50 businesses founded, and over 100 wells drilled. Siblings, Nancy Bruns and Lewis Payne, revived the family business in 2013.
about:
J.Q. Dickinson Salt-Works operates from Charleston, West Virginia, where siblings Nancy Bruns and Lewis Payne revived their family's salt-making legacy in 2013. The Dickinson family had been among the region's largest producers for more than 120 years, during a period when the area led the country in salt output with over 50 businesses and 100 wells. The current incarnation draws on that heritage, positioning itself as an artisan salt company rooted in Appalachian tradition.

The company harvests brine from an ancient ocean deposit sealed beneath the Appalachian Mountains, then slow-sun-dries it in small batches to produce a mineral-rich finishing salt with a distinctive texture. Its product line includes plain heirloom finishing salt, cooking and popcorn salt, grinding salt, and a range of flavored blends such as mushroom herb, bourbon-barrel smoked, bloody mary, and ghost pepper. Beyond salt, the mercantile curates spice blend gift sets, sampler boxes, and other handcrafted pantry and home goods from regional artisans.

Customers include home chefs, gift buyers, and wholesale accounts; the company explicitly invites retailers to carry its products and lists a Faire storefront for trade orders. Its subscription boxes and gift sets target the specialty food and gifting markets, while the salt guide and educational content serve culinary enthusiasts seeking authenticity.

The founders emphasize family heritage, sustainability, and traditional methods as differentiators, stating that every item reflects a commitment to quality and authenticity. By working with artisans who share their values, they aim to keep the spirit of Appalachia alive in each jar and bag.

JATCO Incorporated, a custom plastic injection molding company, was founded in 1976 in Union City, California, in the San Francisco Bay Area. The company later relocated to a larger facility in Modesto, California, where it operates today.

The company provides custom plastic injection molding services including overmolding, as well as die casting, metal stamping, product design, engineering, tooling, assembly, painting, packaging, warehousing, and distribution. JATCO also manufactures and sells its own product lines: concrete cylinder molds under the TestCylinderMolds brand and seedling trays under the Plantway brand. The Modesto plant operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and the company notes operations on two continents.

The company cites long-term production partnerships with firms such as Sony, Tesla, Life Technologies, and Velux.

name: JEM Electronics, Inc.
old_description: We’re far beyond a cable assembly company. We bridge together endless innovative possibilities to see your product come to life
about:
JEM Electronics, Inc. was founded in 1981 in Franklin, Massachusetts, by John McDonald, who remains president and CEO. After years in the wire and cable industry, McDonald saw that custom cable and harness assemblies were still being built with traditional methods.

Today JEM operates as a contract manufacturer specializing in custom cable assemblies, wire harnesses, and electromechanical box-build assemblies. The company runs ISO 9001:2015–certified facilities in Franklin, MA, and Tijuana, Mexico, providing both domestic and near-shore capacity. Every build follows a documented process: drawings are reviewed for manufacturability before quoting, assemblies meet IPC/WHMA-A-620 and IPC-J-STD-001 standards, and 100% of units undergo in-house testing—including continuity, hipot, VSWR, and pull testing—before shipment. Volume ranges from prototype to high-volume production.

JEM serves OEMs in regulated, high-reliability sectors including military and defense (ITAR-registered, CAGE 3DTF7), medical and healthcare, semiconductor equipment, robotics, renewable energy, oil and gas, and networking. The company emphasizes full traceability and on-schedule delivery for applications where cable failure is not an option.

Leadership cites a culture of cross-trained assemblers and Lean Six Sigma continuous improvement that enables flexible staffing and waste reduction. JEM promises transparent quoting grounded in actual component lead times, a manufacturability review that catches terminal or routing issues early, and a commitment to “get builds right the first time, document every step, and stand behind every assembly we ship.”

Founded in 1986, JIT Manufacturing operates from a 32,031-square-foot facility in Woodinville, Washington, just northeast of Seattle along the I-405 corridor. The company began with a focus on precision sheet metal and machined parts for a variety of industries.

The shop provides precision sheet metal fabrication and CNC machining, including laser cutting, forming, punching, welding (AWS D17.2 spot-weld and AWS D1.3 plug-weld certified), and hardware installation such as studs, standoffs, and nuts. Its quality system targets a 98 percent internal and customer acceptance rate and a 98 percent on-time delivery rate, with measuring equipment calibrated to national standards.

The company's stated mission is to be an outstanding precision manufacturer for aerospace, medical, and electronics customers, emphasizing reliability, continuous improvement, and on-time delivery. It highlights quick turnaround, strict quality control, and partnerships with regional finishing houses as key differentiators.

about:
JJISCO, Inc. is headquartered in Oconomowoc, Wisconsin. Its name derives from the founder’s initials combined with “Innovative Solutions Company,” and it was formally formed in 2000 to provide quality material component solutions for OEMs.

The company manufactures custom and standard engineered components from hard materials including silicon carbide, tungsten carbide, and engineered ceramics such as alumina and zirconia. Its product range covers seals, bushings, shafts, nozzles, wear rings, thrust plates, seats, frac plug buttons, burst discs, bearings, mag drive components, rotary steerable system components, and semiconductor parts. JJISCO operates a mid-size facility in southeast Wisconsin capable of both high- and low-volume production, supported by sub-contract assembly, material selection services, and a just-in-time/Kanban inventory system.

The company serves OEMs seeking collaborative partnerships for component design, material selection, and supply chain optimization.

JJISCO differentiates itself through three pillars: Quality Components, backed by ISO 9001:2015 certification and full traceability; Tailored Solutions, involving engineers and technical sales staff in co-developing designs; and Personalized Service, enabled by a nimble footprint that promises fast response times and flexible, customer-specific support.

about:
JUNE Medical USA Inc. is the Delaware-based U.S. entity of JUNE Medical, a privately owned medical device group with offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, and Sweden. The company was founded under the code name "JUNE," chosen to represent spring, growth, and the future, and is led by CEO Angela Spang.

The group manages early-stage innovation, research and development, manufacturing, and global commercialization of surgical devices. Its product portfolio includes the Galaxy II self-retaining surgical retractor, the HandMe retractor for hand surgery, the LUX Connect flexible surgical light, Oxiplex adhesion barriers for intrauterine or peritoneal procedures, and the Thermablate EAS balloon system for heavy menstrual bleeding. Manufacturing is carried out through its sister company, Mosaic Surgical, which also provides UK Authorised Representative services.

JUNE Medical serves surgeons, hospitals, and healthcare systems across more than 40 countries through local partners. In the UK, it supplies the National Health Service (NHS) and private providers such as Circle Health Group, Nuffield Health, and Ramsay Healthcare. Its Swedish subsidiary, JUNE Medical Sverige AB, handles direct sales in Sweden and acts as the EU Authorised Representative for the group's devices.

The company states its purpose is to simplify surgical complexity, improve access to medical devices, build partnerships for safer surgery, and reduce the environmental impact of surgery. Its quality policy emphasizes customer focus, continual improvement, and evidence-based decision-making.

about:
Jerry's Electric was founded in 1976 as a family-owned business serving the utility and industrial electrical sectors. The company operates from a facility just outside Colman, South Dakota, and ships its products throughout the United States and into Canada.

The company remanufactures transformers, voltage regulators, and switchgear, and provides repair, reclamation, and PCB analysis services for oil-filled electrical equipment. Its remanufactured transformers cover single-phase polemount units from 5 to 500 kVA, single-phase padmount units from 10 to 333 kVA, and three-phase substation and padmount transformers up to 10 MVA. All remanufactured transformers are built with new insulating oil, new copper windings, and Kraft diamond-back paper insulation, and carry a three-year warranty. The facility also performs comprehensive inspections, testing, and diagnostics, and uses gas chromatography for PCB oil analysis.

Jerry's Electric serves utility and industrial electrical customers across the U.S. and Canada, offering sale, repair, and recycling solutions for oil-filled transformers and related equipment.

The company emphasizes fast, affordable solutions without sacrificing quality, guided by values that aim to positively impact customers and employees. Its mission centers on delivering high-quality transformers, regulators, switchgear, and repair services with exceptional speed and support.

old_description: Founded in 1961, Jones Plastic & Engineering has spent decades building one of North America’s most integrated plastic manufacturing operations. about:
Jones Plastic & Engineering was founded in 1961 in Louisville, Kentucky, by brothers Harry and Larry Jones as a single-machine operation producing whiskey bottle caps. The family-owned business, now headed by the second and third generations of the Jones family, is based in Jeffersontown, Kentucky, and operates nine facilities across the United States and Mexico.

The company provides integrated plastic manufacturing services, spanning product development, tooling, injection molding (65 to 3,150 tons across five facilities), robotic painting and hydrographics, assembly, and testing. A 90,000-square-foot paint and hydrographics plant in Juárez, Mexico, includes a 25,000-square-foot clean-room line with FANUC robots and a 1.3-meter dip tank. An in-house 3D printing lab runs FDM and PolyJet systems for functional prototypes and short-run molded samples. Total manufacturing space approaches 1.6 million square feet, supported by roughly 3,000 employees. The firm also owns Rev-A-Shelf, a subsidiary producing residential cabinet storage products.

Jones Plastic serves automotive, appliance, powersports, outdoor products, consumer goods, and industrial and defense markets, supplying North American OEMs with components and assemblies that require Class-A cosmetic finishes and tight tolerances.

The company pioneered gas-assist injection molding in the early 1990s and emphasizes an engineering-first approach, using Moldex3D mold-flow analysis and finite element analysis to validate designs before tooling. Integrating molding, finishing, and assembly under one supply chain aims to reduce freight, handling, and coordination costs for near-shore production. Quality management is ISO 9001 certified.

about:
K & F Electronics was founded in 1972 in Fraser, Michigan, a suburb of Detroit. The company remains a third-generation family-owned business, with the founder's grandchildren now overseeing operations. From a single facility, the firm has grown into a full-service provider of printed circuit board fabrication, assembly, and design.

The company produces single-sided, double-sided, and multilayer rigid boards, as well as flex and rigid-flex circuits with blind and buried vias. Materials include FR-4, Rogers, Taconic, Arlon, Nelco, Teflon, polyimide, and aluminum. Assembly services cover surface-mount, through-hole, and box-build work, supported by automated SMT lines rated at 18,000–30,000 components per hour, selective soldering, and hand soldering for special requirements. In-house engineering handles schematic design, PCB layout, bill-of-materials generation, and reverse engineering of existing boards. Additional services include 3D printing of prototypes, wire stripping, conformal coating (acrylic), flying-probe electrical testing, and PCB drilling and routing. All boards pass through a multi-level inspection process that includes AOI, X-ray, and dimensional checks to IPC Class 3.

K & F Electronics serves customers needing quick-turn prototypes and production quantities, offering expedited lead times from 24 hours to four weeks. The firm can begin assembly the same day the final component arrives.

The company emphasizes its integrated design-through-assembly model, a return rate below 1 percent, and a one-year warranty on all PCBs and PCBAs. ITAR registration since 2009 and ISO 9001:2015 certification support work with defense and regulated customers. The family legacy and same-day assembly capability are cited as key differentiators.

about:
KOA Speer Electronics Inc operates from Bradford, Pennsylvania, where it develops and manufactures a range of passive electronic components. The company positions itself as a passive component partner for designers seeking resistors with specialized performance characteristics.

Its product portfolio centers on resistor technologies built for demanding environments. Current sense resistors use a metal plate structure to handle large current detection across multiple sizes, power ratings, and resistance values. The SG73 series of thick film resistors addresses surge and pulse voltage protection, while thin film lines such as RN73R, RN73H, and the wide terminal WN73H deliver high precision for automotive and industrial circuits. Wide terminal chip resistors employ a reverse geometry that improves heat dissipation and enables higher power ratings in the same footprint. Anti-sulfur variants incorporate a sulfuration-proof inner electrode and metal glaze thick film, qualified to AEC-Q200 and ASTM-B809 standards.

The company serves primarily the automotive and industrial electronics sectors, supplying components that meet automotive reliability requirements such as AEC-Q200. Its resistors are designed into power supply protection, circuit control, and high-reliability applications where sulfuration resistance and pulse withstand capability are critical.

KOA Speer differentiates itself through its metal plate current sense technology, wide terminal architecture for thermal performance, and a focus on anti-sulfur solutions that address silver electrode degradation in harsh environments. The firm also emphasizes sample availability for design validation.

old_description: From our humble beginnings in 1927, we have traveled along a sustainable path of growth to become one of the largest originators and marketers of dry edible beans in the world. We are an employee and family owned company that is headquartered in Scottsbluff, Nebraska.
about:
Kelley Bean Co. traces its roots to 1927 when the Chester B. Brown Company was founded in Morrill, Nebraska, with Robert L. Kelley Sr. as plant manager. The business evolved through family leadership: Kelley became president in 1941, then left in 1969 to establish Kelley Bean Co. in Henry, Nebraska, alongside his son Gary. The two entities merged in 1982 under Gary's leadership, and today the company is an employee- and family-owned enterprise headquartered in Scottsbluff, Nebraska, now guided by a fourth generation led by Kevin Kelley.

The company processes and markets dry edible beans — including Pinto, Great Northern, and other varieties — sourced directly from a network of grower partners. Its facilities run a multi-step cleaning line known as 'triple clean': beans pass over round and slot-hole screens for size separation, gravity tables and de-stoners for weight separation, and optical electric-eye sorters that eject off-color or damaged beans by air puff. Additional equipment includes rare-earth magnets, metal detectors, and prewash systems. All plants operate under the internally developed P.A.S.S. System, a GFSI-aligned food safety program, and multiple sites hold GFSI certification and pass annual AIB audits.

Kelley Bean serves food manufacturers, canners, food-service distributors, and retail packers across the U.S. and internationally (notably a 2006 export sale to Cuba).

The firm cites its employee stock ownership plan (launched in 1983), multi-generational family stewardship, and a culture of 'absolute integrity, hard work, dedication, service, and community involvement' as differentiators. The P.A.S.S. System and direct grower traceability are presented as unique safeguards for quality and safety from field to bag.

The customer base includes independent restaurants, delicatessens, institutional kitchens, and retail shoppers. The firm also works with domestic and international suppliers, emphasizing relationships with local farmers and dairy producers.

The Ciocca family’s second generation, Carlo and Danny, now lead the company after Leo’s passing in 2023.

Lima Sheet Metal serves industrial, commercial, and municipal customers throughout Ohio. The firm emphasizes complete in-house control from design through installation, fast turnaround on quotes (within 24 hours), and emergency repair services to minimize downtime. Three generations of the Emerick family oversee a team of certified welders and machinists who maintain rigorous quality standards on every project.

about:
Lincare is headquartered in Rolla, Missouri. The company operates as a family of businesses that includes REMsafe SLEEP®, a sleep apnea solutions provider. No founding year or founders are disclosed in the available sources.

Lincare delivers in-home respiratory care services nationwide, offering home oxygen therapy, sleep apnea treatment (CPAP and BiPAP), nebulizer therapy, home INR testing, and a range of durable medical equipment (DME) including mobility aids and sleep therapy supplies. The company also provides enteral therapy, high-frequency chest wall oscillation, powered mobility devices, long-term care respiratory programs, pediatric services, pharmacy delivery, pulmonary education, speech generating devices, tracheostomy and suction therapy, and both invasive and non-invasive ventilator therapy. Digital tools such as the VentCircle™ mobile app and a secure patient portal support supply ordering, billing, and therapy tracking.

The company serves patients with chronic respiratory conditions, sleep disorders, and congestive heart failure, as well as long-term care facilities and nursing homes. A noted business relationship includes providing sleep apnea treatment to TCW’s fleet of 500 drivers. Lincare distributes equipment from brands such as B Medical (Luna G3, Luna II), Drive Medical (DeVilbiss Traveler Portable Nebulizer, Power Neb Ultra Compressor), Medline Industries (Aeromist Compact Compressor), and Vesco Medical (Q Enteral Feeding Pump).

Lincare states its mission is to set the standard for excellence in home respiratory care, aiming to enable patients with chronic conditions to remain engaged in life. Differentiators include the CareCheck™ COPD early-intervention program, the HeartSteps® congestive heart failure management program, and the SleepEaze™ sleep disorder education and assessment program.

name: Linear Fine Woodworking
old_description: Linear Fine Woodworking provides beautiful custom-built cabinetry and architectural millwork to areas like Phoenix and Scottsdale Arizona as well as the greater Southwest. Each Linear Fine Woodworking creation is a work of art crafted and custom-built just for you. Whether it’s custom designed kitchen cabinetry, a wall unit, home theatre unit, or office furniture, innovation in design and woodworking is a hallmark of Linear Fine Woodworking products.
about:
Linear Fine Woodworking operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where it has been designing and building custom furniture, cabinetry, and architectural millwork for over 30 years. The shop serves clients across Phoenix, Scottsdale, and the broader Southwest region.

The company produces custom cabinetry, architectural millwork, and one-of-a-kind furniture pieces such as kitchen cabinets, wall units, home theater systems, and office furniture. A distinguishing capability is the in-house production of veneer panels from rough-cut flitches, a process that yields uniformly even, stable panels and allows greater design flexibility. The workshop works with exotic veneers, solid woods, glass, integrated lighting, cables, and specialty hardware.

Projects span both residential and commercial sectors.

The firm emphasizes that its in-house veneer manufacturing sets it apart from typical cabinet shops, enabling a level of creativity that blurs the line between functional cabinetry and sculpture. Innovation in design and woodworking is cited as a hallmark of every project.
